title: Shard resequencing causes model identity smear on Console charts
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Symptom: Customer-facing Console charts (top model breakdown, model heatmap, and per-model sparklines) intermittently show 'smearing' where token/usage mass appears briefly under incorrect model aliases after an internal shard resequencing event. This spike is visible for 1-3 buckets and then reconciles after a backfill, causing confusion among customers and triggering support tickets. The effect is most prominent for orgs that use multi-model routing and custom aliases.
reproduction_steps: Run synthetic traffic replay using multi-model routing (models A/B, aliasing enabled) against a sharded ingest pipeline with simulated shard resequencing (out-of-order shard stream + delayed watermark).

Observe per-model aggregate by hour and 5-minute charts. Look for transient re-attribution where tokens attributed to model A briefly show up under model B alias 'unknown-123', then disappear after ingest reconcile job runs.
Enable rate-limit retry fan-in to increase chance of duplicate events and observe smear intensity.
root_cause_summary: The aggregation pipeline uses a two-stage keying approach: fast ingesters assign ephemeral shard-local model identity tokens which are later reconciled during sharded merge. When shard resequencing occurs (e.g., due to consumer rebalance or network hiccup), downstream downsamplers apply time-based windowed smoothing using the ephemeral keys. The smoothing/downsampling logic doesn't wait for final model_id reconciliation, so intermediate aggregates are emitted to the Console with the transient, wrong model key. Backfills correct the model_id, but by then charts already showed the smear and customers saw inconsistent snapshots.
detailed_technical_notes: Ingest path: frontend -> shard writer -> per-shard pre-aggregator -> Kafka topic -> sharded combiner -> downsampler -> materialized timeseries store.

Pre-aggregator emits provisional rows with 'shard_identity' and 'alias_hint' fields. The sharded combiner reconciles to canonical model_id later, but downsampler currently consumes provisional rows and uses smoothing windows of 2-3 buckets for jitter reduction.

Downsampler smoothing algorithm spreads counts across adjacent buckets by shard_identity; it lacks a reconciliation hook to replace provisional key material when the combiner emits the resolved mapping.
Rate-limit retry fan-in duplicates increase frequency of provisional rows with conflicting alias_hint, exacerbating smear.
proposed_fix: Short-term mitigation: Stop emitting to Console from the downsampler for model-identity sensitive metrics until reconciliation completes. Instead, surface a staleness indicator on affected charts (e.g., 'Data may be provisional for the last 15 minutes').

Medium-term: Add reconciliation barrier in the downsampler: buffer provisional rows keyed by shard_identity for a short, configurable watermark (default 60s) and apply reconciliation mappings from the combiner before smoothing/downsampling. This reduces visible provisional attribution while keeping latency targets for most workloads.

Long-term: Move to idempotent event model where each token event carries a canonical model_id assigned at the earliest stable point (frontend or model router). Also consider versioned per-model canonicalization tables persisted to the timeseries store to permit fast retroactive corrections without emitting provisional aggregates to Console.
Implement alerting for sudden per-alias bursts coincident with shard-rebalance traces to allow ops to triage quicker.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic replay tests show 90% reduction in transient mis-attribution events on Console charts under simulated resequencing scenarios.
Console shows a clear staleness indicator for provisional windows and customers no longer receive spike notifications for transient smears.
Metrics: downstream 5m chart latency increase <= 15s compared to baseline after changes, and no increase in 95p tail latency for chart rendering calls.
E2E tests added to replay harness and integrated into CI to prevent regression.
rollback_plan: If customer-visible regressions appear after deployment (increased chart latency or missing real usage), revert the buffer/reconciliation change in the downsampler and re-enable the previous path while toggling a kill-switch feature flag. Notify support and create a postmortem timeline.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the reconciliation buffer in the downsampler.
Deploy to staging and run the synthetic resequencing replay harness. Verify acceptance criteria.
Canary to 10% of traffic (low-traffic region) for 24h and monitor per-model attribution correctness, chart latency, and alert volume.
Gradual ramp to 100% over 72h with monitoring thresholds for automatic rollback.
tests: Unit tests for buffer and reconciliation logic (edge cases: missing mapping, mapping updates, duplicate events).
Integration replay tests in the synthetic harness simulating: normal operation, shard resequence, consumer rebalance, and retry spikes.
Load test to verify default 60s buffer does not cause unacceptable memory pressure at 10k orgs concurrently.
Manual QA: Validate Console charts for several tenant-sized datasets including multi-model routing with alias churn.
notes_and_decisions: 2026-03-05: Initial triage by SRE and Platform team. Reproducible in synthetic harness. Decided to prioritize a buffering reconciliation over removing smoothing entirely to balance latency and correctness.
2026-03-07: PM (Liam Chen) approved user-facing staleness indicator and customer comms plan.
2026-03-09: Design review: added opt-out config for orgs with ultra-low-latency needs. UX to display provisional badge on sparkline tooltip.
customer_communication: Draft support KB created explaining transient attribution artifacts and how backfills correct them. Customer success to proactively reach out to top-10 affected tenants once fix is rolled out.
